title: Day 35 · Week 5, Day 0 — Body: the groove seals and the tube starts to beat — what a scan can see at five, six and seven weeks, and why scanning early for comfort backfires
summary: Week 5 opens with the two structures that matter most. Your baby is about 2 mm today (NHS: a sesame seed), crossing from Carnegie stage 9 to 10, and by the end of the week will be 3–5 mm with 21–29 somite pairs, three pharyngeal arches and the first bulge of an arm. The neural folds fuse from two sites (O'Rahilly & Müller 2002, 98 embryos) and the two neuropores close at stages 11 and 12 — this week and next — which is what the folic acid from Day 29 is for. The heart begins as a straight tube with a pacemaker patch at its inflow and a slow peristaltic wave along it around Day 36–38, then loops to the right and grows five-fold as the chambers bulge (Buijtendijk 2020); the four-chambered version is weeks away. Then the scan: the hCG thresholds and discriminatory levels for sac, yolk sac and embryo (390/3,510; 1,094/17,716; 1,394/47,685 — Connolly 2013), the crown-rump curves that start at 5.5 weeks and the old Robinson curve's 4-day underestimate at 6 weeks (Pexsters 2010; Papaioannou 2010), the heart-rate floor of 100 bpm to 6.2 weeks and 120 at 6.3–7 (Doubilet & Benson 1995). The risk curve once a heartbeat is seen: 9.4% at 6 completed weeks, 4.2% at 7, 1.5% at 8, 0.5% at 9 (Tong 2008, 697 asymptomatic women). And why a scan before six weeks for reassurance backfires: the old cut-offs declared living pregnancies over 4–8% of the time (Abdallah 2011, 1,060 women), the 2013 criteria that replaced them (CRL ≥7 mm, MSD ≥25 mm, the 11- and 14-day rules), the methotrexate warning, and the real reasons for an early scan — bleeding, one-sided pain, ectopic risk — where you go.
action: Find out when the first scan is booked, and why. If nobody ordered it for a medical reason and it falls before Day 42 (six weeks), ask whether it can move to seven or eight weeks and whether it will be transvaginal — one clear scan beats two uncertain ones and a two-week wait. If she has bleeding, one-sided pain, or any history of ectopic pregnancy or tubal surgery, do the opposite: make sure the early scan happens and go with her. Then write her last-menstrual-period date and usual cycle length on the first page of the pregnancy file; the dating conversation starts from those two numbers.
